answer: In this design, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with every result needed before the next step can begin. GPUs can run separate chains for separate clones, but cannot collapse one chain into parallel work; fabricating many timely identities therefore requires many processors and sustained elapsed time. The voyage across each chain is a computational reef for cheap Sybil attacks, while a Wesolowski proof lets a verifier check completion efficiently and anchor identity claims to the delay.
